planting.note: Plant a bare-root or containerized grafted tree in late winter to early spring in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, siting a compatible pollinizer nearby since Hidden Rose is not reliably self-fruitful.

directions: Plant in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, staking young trees and watering deeply through the first two seasons while roots establish. Hidden Rose, also sold as Airlie Red Flesh, was discovered as a chance seedling near Airlie, Oregon, and is unusual for having rose-pink flesh throughout the fruit rather than just a blush near the skin, a trait that holds up well when the fruit is cooked or baked into rosy sauces and pastries. The medium apple has a green-gold skin overlaid with a dusty red-pink flush, and the dense flesh is crisp with a bright, tangy-sweet, berry-like flavor that fresh-eating fans and cider blenders both prize for its color and acidity. Fruit ripens in the second half of the season and keeps reasonably well in cold storage; thin the crop in early summer to improve fruit size and support annual bearing.

directions: Plant in deep, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun, watering deeply and regularly while the young tree establishes. Pink Pearl was bred by Northern California nurseryman Albert Etter and released in 1944, part of a series of hybrids he made specifically to breed pink and red flesh color into eating apples rather than just skin color. The thin greenish-yellow skin, sometimes brushed with a light pink blush, hides vivid magenta-pink flesh that turns heads when the fruit is sliced, and the flavor is notably tart and lively with berry-like, almost strawberry-scented overtones. It ripens mid to late season and is best used fresh, in sauce, or blended into hard cider for both its acidity and its color; the tree bears fairly young and benefits from thinning to keep fruit size up.

directions: Plant in deep, well-drained soil in full sun, staking the young tree and watering deeply through establishment. Kandil Sinap is an old variety from the Black Sea region of Turkey and Crimea, long grown in Ottoman-era orchards and prized for its distinctive elongated, almost conical shape unlike most round apples. The thin yellow skin, often washed with a light red blush on the sun-exposed side, covers dense, crisp white flesh with a mild, honeyed, aromatic flavor and notably low acid for an heirloom. It is a strong keeper that stores well into winter in cool conditions, ripens late in the season, and is grown today mostly by heirloom orchardists and collectors for its history, form, and storage qualities rather than heavy production.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, watering deeply while the young tree establishes and pruning in late winter to maintain an open canopy. Wickson was bred by Albert Etter in Northern California from a cross involving 'Newtown Pippin', selected for a tiny, cherry-sized golden-red crabapple with an extraordinarily high sugar and acid content rather than for fresh eating. Modern craft cider makers seek it out specifically because a small addition of Wickson juice to a blend adds concentrated sweetness, sharp acidity, and aromatic complexity that balance out blander cider apples. The heavy annual crop of small fruit ripens in early to mid fall and the tree also produces a good spring bloom, making it useful as a multi-purpose pollinizer, cider component, and ornamental in a home orchard.

planting.note: Plant a bare-root or containerized grafted tree in late winter to early spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Dolgo is exceptionally cold-hardy and also serves as a reliable pollinizer for other apples and crabapples.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun, watering deeply through establishment and pruning in late winter to open the canopy for good air circulation. Dolgo was introduced from Russia in the early 1900s and became one of the most widely planted crabapples in cold-climate North America for its extreme hardiness, heavy fragrant white spring bloom, and abundant crop of oblong, bright red fruit up to an inch and a half long. The tart, high-pectin fruit sets bright red jelly and cider without added pectin and ripens in late summer, well ahead of most crabapples, so it is often harvested before other apples are even ready. Because it blooms early and profusely over a long window, Dolgo is also planted purely as a pollinizer tree in orchards of standard apples.
